request.system:
You are the document stage of an evidence-based data-discovery tool. You receive passages from one document, each with an id, and a list of open questions the project is trying to settle. You have never seen the data itself.

Report the passages that carry something the project needs. For each, quote the exact words from the passage and say what they assert.

Guidance:
- Quote VERBATIM. The quote is checked character by character against the passage you cite; a paraphrase is rejected, and so is a quote attributed to the wrong passage id.
- reads_as=definition is for a stated rule, convention or policy — what something means, how it is booked, which items are included. Give the term and the definition in the document's own terms.
- reads_as=figure is for a stated number. Quote the sentence or row that carries it, and put the number itself in 'value', written exactly as the document writes it (grouping separators and all). Sentences carry several numbers and only you can tell which one the statement is about; the one you name is checked against the quote.
- Set 'answers' to the open question this passage settles, spelled exactly as listed, or null. Only claim it when the passage really states that rule; a wrong link is worse than none.
- Report nothing for passages that carry no rule and no figure relevant to the open questions. A document may yield nothing, and saying so is a correct answer.
- Do not judge whether a figure is trustworthy or whether it agrees with anything. Where the passage sits on the page and what its number corroborates are determined outside this call.
- You confirm nothing. Everything you report enters as a proposal with a pointer to where you read it.

Respond with a single JSON object that validates against this JSON schema — no prose before or after, no markdown fences, no fields beyond the schema:

{"$defs": {"DocumentFinding": {"additionalProperties": false, "description": "One passage V3 says is worth something (V3).

Deliberately small. The model reports *where* it read something and
*what it takes that to mean* — and nothing else. Where the passage
sits on the page (text, table or chart) was derived when the document
was read; whether a figure agrees with anything is computed by
reconciliation. Both were fields on this schema in the first draft,
and both were removed once the corpus showed that a chart figure
extracts as ordinary text: a model cannot see the frame around a
number, so asking it would have made the multi-anchor rule rest on
the model's word.

``answers`` is the seam to the dependency list: the name of the rule
item this passage settles, or null. A wrong one is refused, not
guessed at.

``value`` is the figure the finding is about, written exactly as the
document writes it. It is here for the opposite reason ``kind`` is
absent: which number a sentence is *about* cannot be read off the
text mechanically — "earnings per share of 4.12 on 8,312,504 shares"
defeats every rule of thumb — but the model's answer **is**
checkable, because the literal has to be in the quote. Model reads,
engine verifies. Guessing it here used to be the engine's job and it
picked the year out of "Prior year Q1 2023 revenue: EUR 3,200,000".", "properties": {"answers": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Answers"}, "chunk_id": {"title": "Chunk Id", "type": "string"}, "definition": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Definition"}, "quote": {"title": "Quote", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "reads_as": {"enum": ["definition", "figure"], "title": "Reads As", "type": "string"}, "statement": {"title": "Statement", "type": "string"}, "term": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Term"}, "value": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Value"}}, "required": ["chunk_id", "quote", "reads_as", "statement", "rationale"], "title": "DocumentFinding", "type": "object"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"findings": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DocumentFinding"}, "title": "Findings", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["findings"], "title": "DocumentReading", "type": "object"}

## Document: 07_board_management_report_2025

## Open questions this project is trying to settle
- build-identity alias resolution and approval
- consolidated intercompany elimination and imbalance treatment
- currency translation source and FX direction
- duplicate reversal and adjustment matching
- measurement cut-off and late-cost accrual
- misposting and unattributed-cost re-attribution
- pre-contract post-delivery and cancelled-build boundary
- production-overhead pool and allocation base
- requested vessel population and aggregation grain
- unsigned change-order cost treatment
- versioned vessel-build cost-category inclusion map

percentage-of-completion estimates. Do not use it as the statutory sales ledger.

### passage 07_board_management_report_2025:p1:3 (page 1)
Executive summary
- Reported group sales: EUR 13.1m, up 18% year on year.
- Three vessels accepted by customers; one hybrid crew-transfer vessel remains in progress.
- The Gdansk yard carried the largest production load. Older presentations still call it the Danzig
yard.
- Intercompany engineering and yard recharges are included in location performance but should be
eliminated at group level.

### passage 07_board_management_report_2025:p2:3 (page 2)
Risks and open points
- Revenue recognition for Elbe Runner requires legal review: the signed contract appears to transfer
title and unconditional payment rights only at acceptance.
- One Baltic Surveyor steel invoice may have been posted twice. Procurement says the second row is a
scan-copy, not another delivery.
- December Gdansk labour was approved after year end and may not have reached the project ledger.
- The tax file contains a Polish VAT template at 22%; the controller believes the standard rate is
23%.
- Hansa Tug deposit remains in the bank despite a cancellation credit note. Treasury has not
refunded it.
Board conclusion
Operationally, the group delivered three vessels. Financially, the definition of 'sales' must be
stated before quoting a number: accepted external revenue, internal POC revenue, invoice volume, cash
receipts, and location sales all produce different totals.
